questions.q: What does the summary say about your parents' influence on how you handle money?
a: You tend to copy their income strategies without realizing it
Their habits have no effect on your finances
You always reject the way they handled money
Their income determines exactly what you will earn
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares money habits to a family cake recipe, passed down and repeated without question.

questions.q: What does the bus metaphor in the summary illustrate?
a: You are the driver of your finances, not a passenger
Saving money requires giving up the bus
Most expenses are impossible to control
Public transport costs more than driving
questions.why: Lesson 2 says people watch their dollars leave as if someone else were driving, when they are actually in charge.

questions.q: What is the first step to taking control of your money?
a: Realizing that you are the one in charge
Finding a better-paying job
Cutting up all your credit cards
Blaming the economy less often
questions.why: Lesson 2 says recognizing that you sit in the driver's seat is what makes change possible.

questions.q: What does the summary say about despising rich people?
a: It blocks you from becoming rich yourself
It is a healthy way to stay modest
It has no effect on your finances
It helps you avoid bad investments
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that envy and mistrust of the wealthy keep you from learning what they could teach you.

questions.q: What attitude toward wealth does the summary recommend?
a: A positive one that lets you learn from wealthy people
Complete indifference to money and status
Suspicion of anyone who is successful
A desire to display your wealth openly
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a positive attitude toward money is a prerequisite for attracting it, without needing to show off.
